stem.en: Iron filings are mixed with sulfur powder. Both are solids. Which plan separates them, and what difference does it use?

text.en: Hold a magnet over the mixture. Iron is attracted and sulfur is not, so the difference used is magnetism.
Pour the mixture into a separating funnel. Iron is denser, so it will drain first.
Leave the mixture to stand for a day. The two solids will form two layers.
Shake the mixture hard. The lighter solid will rise to the top and can be poured away.

explanation.en: A magnet pulls the iron and leaves the sulfur, so it uses a property that only one of the solids has. A separating funnel needs two liquids, because powders cannot flow as layers past a stopcock. Density is a real difference between iron and sulfur, which makes that plan reasonable, but dry powders standing in a pile do not sort into layers by themselves.

hints.en: Which property does only one of these solids have?
A funnel works on which kind of mixture?
